tweets.text:
Here are 9 vibe coding tips for building with @GoogleAIStudio and Gemini: 

1. Be specific: The more details you give, the more control you have on the final output.

2. Break it down: Work incrementally, step by step, feature by feature.

3. Iterate & refine: Your first prompt will not be perfect. Treat it as a conversation.

4. Use references: Give the model sketches or images as references. Specify font names and styles for more precision.

5. Lean on the model: The model can also help with ideation and prompt refinement.

6. You can revert or restart: If your code assistant requests seem to be hallucinating, use the reset chat option.

7. Patience is key: Things might break, or not work as expected, or take lots of tweaking.

8. It is not deterministic: Opening 3 tabs and submitting the same prompt will yield 3 different outputs.

9. Have fun: Enjoy the process of co-creating with AI as your creative partner.

tweets.text:
A trick that can distinguish a good trader from an average trader can even change our lives. If you're trading on @Polymarket, we need to know the vibe coding approach. Many of you are already familiar with the saying: if we understand how to use this system on Polymarket, we can profit. Also, don't forget to increase volume with @polymaker_bot for the Polymarket airdrop.

Vibe coding means acting with emotion rather than logic, operating with emotional or aesthetic intuition. Understanding how and when this concept can be dangerous, or sometimes advantageous, on a data driven platform like Polymarket will save us money. Of course, we need to use it correctly at the right time.

Every trade on Polymarket is essentially a probability estimate. In other words, the "YES" and "NO" prices indicate the likelihood of an event occurring. Here, the rational trader determines the price based on data and a model.
The vibe coder, on the other hand, takes a position based on "sentiment," not "data."

When trading on a prediction like "ETH will reach $5,000 in November," users we call vibe coders think, "I think people believe in ETH, so YES will increase." Unfortunately, this isn't a logical approach.

vibe coding can be very useful when social momentum is captured early. Some markets, especially meme-worthy topics, start to rise on Twitter or Reddit but are slow to be reflected in the Polymarket price. In this case, the vibe can actually be an early signal.

If you spend a lot of time in the market during the day, your sentiment can be used as an early warning system. However, trading decisions must be validated with data. If price and volume go against the "vibe," that vibe is just noise.

Thinking of the Polymarket as a standard dex doesn't make sense, and taking our trades accordingly can be detrimental. Therefore, understanding the metrics better and trading from a different perspective will be much more profitable.
